mainTopic: The view of אחרים on slaughtering the פסח for מולים and ערלים, explained by רבה and then by אביי, and a new משנה on slaughtering a קרבן while owning חמץ.
overview: The amud opens by explaining the view of אחרים, who are רבי מאיר. When someone slaughters the פסח for both מולים and ערלים, אחרים say the result depends on which group he mentioned first. The גמרא first suggests that שחיטה counts only at its end and that the first words spoken decide, following רבא. רבה rejects this. He says the case is about someone who meant both groups but only managed to say 'ערלים', so the dispute is about פיו ולבו שוים, whether mouth and heart must match. The גמרא challenges רבה from a סתם משנה in תרומות, which follows רבי מאיר and requires mouth and heart to match. אביי therefore explains the case differently: the slaughterer divided his intentions between the two סימנים. Seen this way, the dispute matches the known מחלוקת about whether a קרבן can become פיגול through חצי מתיר. A new משנה then teaches the לאו against slaughtering a קרבן while owning חמץ, including רבי שמעון's rule that one is חייב only when the קרבן is valid. The גמרא begins with ריש לקיש's ruling about whose חמץ counts, and his statement continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A proposed reason for the view of אחרים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that אחרים hold two things. First, שחיטה only counts at its end. Second, like רבא, we follow the first words spoken, even when a person clearly meant his words to apply one after the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say that אחרים hold that שחיטה only counts at the end, and that they agree with רבא. רבא said: the argument is still there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible explanation for why אחרים say the order of 'מולים' and 'ערלים' makes a difference. This step sets up a conclusion that comes in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two ideas are joined together here. The first is that the whole שחיטה is judged at one moment, not over the time it takes. The second is רבא's point that רבי מאיר's rule of 'follow the first words' applies even when the speaker clearly meant each word for a different part of time. Together, these mean that only the first group mentioned can count.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say. This introduces a suggested explanation that may later be rejected.
'Others.' This is a name used for רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
The שְׁחִיטָה only counts at its end, not throughout.
It is still a dispute. רָבָא's point that the argument applies even in this case.

steps.confusionAlert: אחרים here is not an unknown group of people. It is a name for רבי מאיר. Keep this in mind, because later the גמרא will compare this view with another statement of רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: Let us say that Acherim hold
that slaughter does not count except at the end,
phrases.notes: The slaughter is judged at a single moment.

phrases.english: and in line with Rava.
For Rava said:
It is still a dispute.
phrases.notes: The 'first words count' argument applies even when he clearly meant his words to take effect one after the other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the analysis of the opinion of אחרים in the ברייתא about the פסח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proposed: אחרים hold that שחיטה counts only at the end, and they follow רבא, who says the first words govern.

steps.title: The result: whichever group is mentioned first takes effect
steps.stepSummary: Based on the suggestion in step 1, whichever group the slaughterer names first is the one that counts. The second group does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore: if he put מולים before ערלים, the מולים take effect and the ערלים do not. If he put ערלים before מולים, the ערלים take effect and the מולים do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the suggestion by showing how it produces the ruling of אחרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שחיטה is judged at one moment, and only the first words count. So whichever group was named first decides the status of the קרבן. If ערלים came first, the פסח is פסול. If מולים came first, it is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore.
He put first. He mentioned this group before the other.
Circumcised people, who are allowed to eat the פֶּסַח.
Uncircumcised people. Slaughtering the פֶּסַח for them makes it פָּסוּל.
Take effect.

phrases.english: Therefore:
if he put the circumcised before the uncircumcised,
the circumcised take effect, the uncircumcised do not take effect.
If he put the uncircumcised before the circumcised,
the uncircumcised take effect, the circumcised do not take effect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the practical result of the suggestion in step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Under this suggestion, only the first group named counts.

steps.title: רבה rejects the suggestion and redefines the case
steps.stepSummary: רבה says no. אחרים agree that שחיטה counts from beginning to end. The case is about someone who intended both groups, but the שחיטה was finished after he had said only 'ערלים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: No. Really, אחרים hold that שחיטה counts from start to finish. What case are we dealing with here? Someone who decided in his heart on both groups, מולים and ערלים. He said out loud 'for ערלים', but he did not manage to say 'for מולים' before the שחיטה was already finished while he was still on 'ערלים'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה pushes away the suggestion from steps 1–2. He gives a different, narrower picture of the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה keeps the normal rule that שחיטה counts the whole time it is happening. He explains the ruling of אחרים through a timing problem instead. The person meant both groups, but only the word 'ערלים' was actually spoken during the שחיטה. This changes the question. It is no longer about which words came first. It is about whether his unspoken intent for מולים counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth. Used to reject a suggestion and keep the basic assumption.
The שְׁחִיטָה counts from beginning to end.
With what case are we dealing here? This introduces a narrower case.
He decided in his heart.
He did not manage, he did not have time.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבה here with רבא in step 1. These are two different אמוראים, and רבה is arguing against the suggestion that relied on רבא.

phrases.english: Rabbah said: No,
really, Acherim hold
that slaughter counts from beginning to end,
and with what are we dealing here?
For example, where he decided in his heart on both of them,
both for circumcised and for uncircumcised,
and he expressed with his mouth 'for uncircumcised,'
but did not manage to say 'for circumcised'
before the slaughter was finished on 'uncircumcised.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: לָא, לְעוֹלָם קָסָבְרִי אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the explanation in steps 1–2 and replaces it with a new case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that אחרים hold שחיטה counts only at its end.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is no need to change the normal rule of שחיטה. The ruling can be explained by a specific timing case.

steps.title: The real dispute: must mouth and heart match
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds we do not need the mouth and heart to match, so the spoken word 'ערלים' makes the פסח פסול. The רבנן hold they must match, so it stays כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what they argue about. רבי מאיר holds that we do not need his mouth and heart to be the same. The רבנן hold that we do need his mouth and heart to be the same.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה states the exact point of the dispute within the case he just described.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, what was actually said decides the matter. He said only 'ערלים', so the פסח is פסול. For the רבנן, speech counts only when it matches what the person really meant. Since he meant both groups, the word 'ערלים' alone does not make the פסח פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what they argue about.
His mouth and heart match. What he says must match what he means.
We do not need, we do not require.
The Sages, the majority opinion.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה: רבי מאיר says what is spoken counts even without matching intent, and the רבנן require mouth and heart to match.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next challenge. If רבי מאיר does not require פיו ולבו שוים, any source where he does require it would contradict רבה.

phrases.english: And on this they disagree:
Rabbi Meir holds:
we do not require that his mouth and heart be the same.
And the Rabbis hold:
we require that his mouth and heart be the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבה's explanation by naming the principle behind the dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: פיו ולבו שוים is not required. רבנן: it is required.

steps.title: Does רבי מאיר really not require mouth and heart to match
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised by רבה's claim about רבי מאיר and announces a contradiction from another source.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי מאיר really hold that we do not need his mouth and heart to be the same? Let us compare it with another source:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבה's description of רבי מאיר. It is introducing a contradicting source, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The target is the claim from step 4 that רבי מאיר does not require פיו ולבו שוים. The word ורמינהו tells us a contradicting text is about to be quoted.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contrasted them. This introduces a source that contradicts what was just said.
And does he hold...? Here it expresses surprise.

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Meir hold
that we do not require his mouth and heart to be the same?
Raise a contradiction:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָסָבַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר לָא בָּעֵינַן פִּיו וְלִבּוֹ שָׁוִין? וּרְמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבה's description of רבי מאיר in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that רבי מאיר does not require פיו ולבו שוים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another source attributed to רבי מאיר does require mouth and heart to match.

steps.title: The משנה in תרומות that requires mouth and heart to match
steps.stepSummary: A משנה rules that if someone meant one thing and said another, his words mean nothing until mouth and heart match. Since an unattributed משנה follows רבי מאיר, this contradicts רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone meant to say 'תרומה' and said 'מעשר', or meant 'מעשר' and said 'תרומה'. Or he meant to vow 'I will not enter this house' and said 'that one', or 'I will not benefit from this person' and said 'that one'. He has said nothing until his mouth and heart are the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the contradicting משנה, completing the challenge against רבה that began in step 5. The גמרא gives no answer for רבה. Instead, in the next step אביי drops רבה's explanation entirely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In every example, a slip of the tongue does not take effect, because speech without matching intent does not count. The rule is that a סתם משנה, a משנה with no name on it, follows רבי מאיר. So it looks as if רבי מאיר does require פיו ולבו שוים, which is the opposite of what רבה said.

keyTerms.meaning: One who intended to say.
The portion of produce given to a כֹּהֵן.
Tithe, a tenth of the produce.
That I will not benefit. The language of a vow.
He has said nothing. His words have no legal effect.

steps.confusionAlert: The name רבי מאיר does not appear in this משנה. The contradiction works only because of the rule that a סתם משנה follows רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: One who intended to say 'teruma'
but said 'tithe';
or intended 'tithe' but said 'teruma';
or intended 'that I will not enter this house'
but said 'that one';
or 'that I will not benefit from this one,' but said 'from that one'
has not said anything
until his mouth and heart are the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source text for the contradiction announced in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר requires פיו ולבו שוים, which contradicts רבה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: An unattributed משנה in מסכת תרומות, presumed to follow רבי מאיר.

steps.title: אביי explains the two cases as two separate cuts
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the case is about intention during each סימן. In the רישא, מולין are included in both cuts. In the סיפא, the first cut was only for ערלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: In the first case he said, 'The first סימן is for מולין, and the second סימן is also for ערלים.' So מולין are included in the second סימן as well. In the second case he said, 'The first סימן is for ערלים, the second סימן for מולין.' So in the first סימן, מולין are not included at all.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רבה's answer was contradicted, אביי gives a different way to explain the ברייתא. He says the slaughterer split his intentions between the two cuts of the שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A proper שחיטה cuts two סימנים, the windpipe and the food pipe. In the רישא, מולין were in his mind for both cuts, so no part of the שחיטה was only for ערלים. In the סיפא, the whole first cut was only for ערלים, so half the שחיטה was done with a bad intention.

keyTerms.meaning: One of the two pipes (windpipe or food pipe) cut in שחיטה
The first part of a ברייתא or משנה
The last part of a ברייתא or משנה
Mixed in, included
Circumcised people / uncircumcised people (ערלים may not eat the פסח)

steps.confusionAlert: The word אלא means אביי is dropping רבה's explanation completely. He is not adding to it.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
phrases.notes: אביי is offering a new explanation in place of רבה's.

phrases.english: The first clause: where he said,
'The first organ for circumcised people,
and the second organ also for uncircumcised people' —
so that in the second organ too
circumcised people are included in it.
The latter clause: where he said,
'The first organ for uncircumcised people,
the second organ for circumcised people' —
so that in the first organ
circumcised people are not included in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבה's explanation, which the משנה in step 6 contradicted
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was about mouth and heart not matching, as רבה said
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about intentions divided between the two סימנים, so it has nothing to do with mouth and heart

steps.title: The dispute depends on disqualifying with half the slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds פיגול can happen with half of the act that permits the קרבן, so the סיפא is פסול. The רבנן disagree, so it is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר follows his own reasoning, since he says: we can make a קרבן פיגול with half of what permits it. And the רבנן follow their reasoning, since they say: we cannot make it פיגול with half of what permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his answer by showing that רבי מאיר and the רבנן are each following an opinion they already hold elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting one סימן is only half of the act that makes the קרבן permitted. רבי מאיר says a bad intention during that half is enough to ruin the קרבן, so a first cut only for ערלים makes it פסול. The רבנן say a bad intention ruins it only if it covers the whole permitting act, so the קרבן stays כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Make a קרבן פיגול, disqualified by a wrong intention
Half of the act that permits the קרבן (for example, one סימן out of two)
Following his own known reasoning

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, the ערלים ברייתא is not about mouth and heart matching. It is the known מחלוקת of whether you can disqualify a קרבן with חצי מתיר, so there is no contradiction with רבי מאיר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is how אביי escapes the contradiction from step 6. רבי מאיר can still require mouth and heart to match, and still rule the סיפא פסול.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir follows his reasoning, as he says:
piggul status can be conferred at half of what permits it.
And the Rabbis follow their reasoning, as they say:
piggul status cannot be conferred at half of what permits it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's answer by giving the legal reason behind each opinion
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking the dispute to a known underlying מחלוקת
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר holds מפגלין בחצי מתיר, and the רבנן hold אין מפגלין בחצי מתיר

steps.title: New משנה: slaughtering a sacrifice while owning leaven on the fourteenth
steps.stepSummary: Slaughtering the פסח while owning חמץ breaks a לא תעשה. רבי יהודה adds the תמיד. רבי שמעון says that on the fourteenth, only a valid פסח (לשמו) makes one חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who slaughters the פסח while owning חמץ breaks a לא תעשה. רבי יהודה says: even the תמיד. רבי שמעון says: For the פסח on the fourteenth, if slaughtered לשמו he is חייב; שלא לשמו he is פטור. For all other קרבנות, whether לשמן or שלא לשמן, he is פטור.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic. It covers the איסור of slaughtering a קרבן while you still own חמץ, starting with the fourteenth of ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'לא תשחט על חמץ דם זבחי' forbids this. רבי יהודה extends it to the afternoon תמיד of ערב פסח. רבי שמעון holds that on the fourteenth the איסור covers only the פסח, and only when it is a valid קרבן. A פסח brought לשמו is valid, but a פסח brought שלא לשמו on that day is פסול, so he is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: While חמץ is still in one's possession
A negative commandment
The daily communal קרבן (here, the afternoon one)
Slaughtered for its own type of קרבן / for a different type
Liable to punishment / exempt

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי שמעון's main idea is that you are חייב only if the קרבן you slaughtered is valid. This idea explains every ruling in the rest of the משנה.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who slaughters the Paschal lamb with leaven in his possession —
violates a negative commandment.
Rabbi Yehuda says: even the daily offering.
Rabbi Shimon says:
the Paschal lamb on the fourteenth, for its own purpose — he is liable;
and for a different purpose — he is exempt.
And all other offerings,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לִשְׁמָן וּבֵין שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן — פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: whether for their own purpose or for a different purpose — he is exempt.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering the פסח while owning חמץ breaks a לא תעשה. רבי יהודה includes the תמיד. רבי שמעון: on the fourteenth, only a פסח slaughtered לשמו makes one חייב.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's rulings for the festival days themselves
steps.stepSummary: During the מועד the results flip. A פסח לשמו is פטור and a פסח שלא לשמו is חייב. All other קרבנות are חייב, except a חטאת slaughtered שלא לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And during the מועד: the פסח לשמו, he is פטור; שלא לשמו, he is חייב. And all other קרבנות, whether לשמן or שלא לשמן, he is חייב. The exception is a חטאת that he slaughtered שלא לשמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues רבי שמעון's opinion and applies it to the days of פסח itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the מועד it is the wrong time for a פסח, so a פסח brought לשמו is פסול and he is פטור. A פסח brought שלא לשמו turns into a valid שלמים, so he is חייב. Other קרבנות stay valid either way, so he is חייב. The one exception is a חטאת, which becomes פסול when brought שלא לשמה, so he is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: The festival days of פסח themselves
Sin-offering, which becomes פסול when slaughtered שלא לשמה
Except for

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון the rule is always the same: חייב only when the קרבן slaughtered is valid. That is why the פסח's results flip between the fourteenth and the מועד.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not memorize the flipped results as random. Each time, simply ask whether this קרבן is valid on this day with this intention.

phrases.english: And during the festival, for its own purpose — he is exempt.
For a different purpose — he is liable.
And all other offerings,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לִשְׁמָן בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן — חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: whether for their own purpose or for a different purpose — he is liable.
Except for the sin-offering
that he slaughtered for a different purpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי שמעון's opinion, moving from the fourteenth to the festival days
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During the מועד: a פסח לשמו is פטור and שלא לשמו is חייב. Other קרבנות are always חייב, except a חטאת slaughtered שלא לשמה.

steps.title: The חמץ must belong to the slaughterer or the sprinkler
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש begins to define whose חמץ makes one חייב: the one who does the שחיטה or the זריקה. His sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: A person is never חייב unless the חמץ belongs to the one who slaughters or to the one who sprinkles the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining the משנה. ריש לקיש tells us whose חמץ counts for this לאו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that slaughtering the פסח while owning חמץ breaks a לא תעשה, but it did not say whose חמץ counts. ריש לקיש narrows it down, starting with the people doing the עבודה: the שוחט or the זורק. His sentence is not finished on this amud. It continues on the next amud and adds another case.

keyTerms.meaning: ריש לקיש, a major אמורא of ארץ ישראל
He is never liable
The one who slaughters the קרבן
The one who sprinkles the blood on the מזבח
Leavened bread

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that any חמץ anywhere makes the slaughterer חייב. ריש לקיש limits whose חמץ counts. His list starts here with the שוחט and the זורק and continues on the next amud, so do not treat these two as the complete list.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic limit of the לאו, and the rest of the גמרא will build on it and question it.

phrases.english: GEMARA
phrases.notes: The start of the גמרא on this משנה

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
One is never liable
phrases.notes: Liable for breaking the לאו of 'לא תשחט על חמץ'.

phrases.english: unless the leavened bread belongs to the one who slaughters
or to the one who sprinkles
phrases.notes: The one doing the זריקת הדם

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: לְעוֹלָם אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה cited in Steps 9-10 by defining whose חמץ creates liability.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability for slaughtering the פסח while owning חמץ applies only when the חמץ belongs to certain people. The list begins with the שוחט and the זורק and continues on the next amud.
